+"""Tests for the interactive CLI chat."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import re
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from typing import Any
+
+from typer.testing import CliRunner
+
+from cli.chat import (
+    ChatConfig,
+    ChatSession,
+    _normalize_tool_calls,
+    _to_openai_tools,
+    handle_command,
+)
+from cli.cli import app
+
+ANSI_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\x1b\[[0-9;]*m")
+
+
+def _strip_ansi(text: str) -> str:
+    return ANSI_ESCAPE.sub("", text)
+
+
+def _config() -> ChatConfig:
+    return ChatConfig(
+        base_url="http://localhost:8001/v1",
+        api_key="local",
+        model="test-model",
+        mcp_url="http://localhost:8000/mcp",
+    )
+
+
+class _FakeSession:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.tool_names = ["add_job", "get_jobs"]
+        self.cleared = False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.cleared = True
+
+
+class _FakeStream:
+    def __init__(self, chunks: list[Any]) -> None:
+        self._chunks = list(chunks)
+
+    def __aiter__(self) -> _FakeStream:
+        return self
+
+    async def __anext__(self) -> Any:
+        if not self._chunks:
+            raise StopAsyncIteration
+        return self._chunks.pop(0)
+
+
+class _FakeCompletions:
+    def __init__(self, streams: list[_FakeStream]) -> None:
+        self._streams = list(streams)
+        self.calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+
+    async def create(self, **kwargs: Any) -> _FakeStream:
+        self.calls.append(kwargs)
+        return self._streams.pop(0)
+
+
+class _FakeMCP:
+    def __init__(self, tools: list[Any], results: dict[str, str]) -> None:
+        self._tools = tools
+        self._results = results
+        self.calls: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
+
+    async def list_tools(self) -> list[Any]:
+        return self._tools
+
+    async def call_tool(self, name: str, arguments: dict[str, Any]) -> Any:
+        self.calls.append((name, arguments))
+        return SimpleNamespace(content=[SimpleNamespace(text=self._results[name])])
+
+
+def _chunk(content: str | None = None, tool_calls: list[Any] | None = None) -> Any:
+    delta = SimpleNamespace(content=content, tool_calls=tool_calls)
+    return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(delta=delta)])
+
+
+def _make_session(
+    streams: list[_FakeStream], tools: list[Any], results: dict[str, str]
+) -> tuple[ChatSession, _FakeCompletions, _FakeMCP]:
+    completions = _FakeCompletions(streams)
+    openai_client = SimpleNamespace(chat=SimpleNamespace(completions=completions))
+    mcp = _FakeMCP(tools, results)
+    session = ChatSession(_config(), openai_client, mcp)
+    return session, completions, mcp
+
+
+def test_chat_help_lists_connection_options() -> None:
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    result = runner.invoke(app, ["chat", "--help"])
+
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
+    output = _strip_ansi(result.output)
+    assert "--base-url" in output
+    assert "--model" in output
+    assert "--mcp-url" in output
+
+
+def test_no_args_without_tty_prints_help() -> None:
+    runner = CliRunner()
+    result = runner.invoke(app, ["--no-update"])

+    assert "Usage" in _strip_ansi(result.output)

+    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY", "secret")

+
+    config = ChatConfig.from_env(model="from-flag")
+
+    assert config.model == "from-flag"
+
+
+def test_handle_command_routes_and_clears(capsys) -> None:
+    session = _FakeSession()
+
+    assert handle_command("hello", session) is None
+    assert handle_command("/exit", session) == "exit"
+    assert handle_command("/quit", session) == "exit"
+    assert handle_command("/help", session) == "handled"
+    assert handle_command("/tools", session) == "handled"
+    assert handle_command("/clear", session) == "handled"
+    assert session.cleared is True
+    assert handle_command("/nope", session) == "handled"
+
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert "add_job" in output
+    assert "Unknown command" in output
+
+
+def test_to_openai_tools_translates_fastmcp_schema() -> None:
+    tool = SimpleNamespace(
+        name="add_job",
+        description=None,
+        input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+    )
+
+    assert _to_openai_tools([tool]) == [
+        {
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {
+                "name": "add_job",
+                "description": "",
+                "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+            },
+        }
+    ]
+
+
+def test_normalize_tool_calls_fills_missing_id_and_arguments() -> None:
+    calls = _normalize_tool_calls({0: {"id": "", "name": "get_jobs", "arguments": ""}})
+
+    assert calls == [
+        {
+            "id": "call_0",
+            "type": "function",
+            "function": {"name": "get_jobs", "arguments": "{}"},
+        }
+    ]
+

+def test_session_streams_the_answer_and_executes_tool_calls() -> None:
+    tool_start = SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id="call-1",
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name="add_job", arguments='{"name": '),
+    )
+    tool_arguments = SimpleNamespace(
+        index=0,
+        id=None,
+        function=SimpleNamespace(name=None, arguments='"Test"}'),
+    )
+    first = _FakeStream(
+        [
+            _chunk(content="Let me add that. ", tool_calls=[tool_start]),
+            _chunk(tool_calls=[tool_arguments]),
+        ]
+    )
+    second = _FakeStream([_chunk(content="Added the job.")])
+    tools = [
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            name="add_job",
+            description="Add a job",
+            input_schema={"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}}},
+        )
+    ]
+    session, completions, mcp = _make_session(
+        [first, second], tools, {"add_job": '{"id": "job-1"}'}
+    )
+
+    asyncio.run(session.initialize())
+    pieces: list[str] = []
+    reply = asyncio.run(session.ask("Add a job named Test", on_delta=pieces.append))
+
+    assert reply == "Added the job."
+    assert "".join(pieces) == "Let me add that. Added the job."
+    assert mcp.calls == [("add_job", {"name": "Test"})]
+    assert completions.calls[0]["stream"] is True
+    assert any(
+        message.get("role") == "tool" and message.get("content") == '{"id": "job-1"}'
+        for message in session.messages
+    )
+
+
+def test_session_rolls_back_failed_turn() -> None:
+    class _BoomCompletions:
+        async def create(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
+            raise RuntimeError("boom")
+
+    openai_client = SimpleNamespace(chat=SimpleNamespace(completions=_BoomCompletions()))
+    session = ChatSession(_config(), openai_client, _FakeMCP([], {}))
+    before = list(session.messages)
+
+    try:
+        asyncio.run(session.ask("hello"))
+    except RuntimeError as exc:
+        assert str(exc) == "boom"
+    else:  # pragma: no cover - the fake always raises
+        raise AssertionError("expected RuntimeError")
+
+    assert session.messages == before
+
+
+def test_session_clear_drops_history() -> None:
+    session, _, _ = _make_session([], [], {})
+    session.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "hello"})
+
+    session.clear()
+
+    assert len(session.messages) == 1
+    assert session.messages[0]["role"] == "system"

+    async def __aenter__(self) -> _FakeMCP:

+    async def __aexit__(self, *exc: Any) -> bool:

+        return self._tools
+

+"""Guard against importing heavy dependencies at CLI module load time.
+
+``agentic-odi --version`` and ``--help`` must not pull in the MCP client,
+the connectors package, or the core domain layer just to run.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import subprocess
+import sys
+
+_HEAVY_MODULES = ("fastmcp", "connectors", "core", "openai")
+
+
+def test_importing_cli_entrypoint_does_not_load_heavy_modules():
+    code = (
+        "import sys; import cli.cli; "
+        "print(','.join(m for m in "
+        f"{list(_HEAVY_MODULES)!r} if m in sys.modules))"
+    )
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
+        capture_output=True,
+        text=True,
+        check=True,
+    )
+    loaded = [name for name in result.stdout.strip().split(",") if name]
+    assert loaded == [], f"heavy modules imported at load time: {loaded}"

+def _make_archive(tmp_path: Path, version: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
+    payload = tmp_path / "stage" / version / "odi"
+    payload.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
+    payload.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho odi")
+    archive = tmp_path / f"odi_{version}_linux_x86_64.tar.gz"
+    with tarfile.open(archive, "w:gz") as tf:
+        tf.add(payload.parent, arcname=".")
+    sha = hashlib.sha256(archive.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+    return archive, sha

+    archive, sha = _make_archive(tmp_path, "0.2.0")
+    root = tmp_path / "install"

+    assert version_dir == root / "versions" / "0.2.0"
+    assert (root / "current").resolve() == version_dir.resolve()
+    assert (version_dir / "odi").exists()

+    archive, _ = _make_archive(tmp_path, "0.2.0")
+    with pytest.raises(update.UpdateError):

+        info.size = len(payload)

+"""
+run.py — Local dev launcher for Agentic ODI.
+
+Starts the FastMCP server (``python -m mcp_server``) and the Living Studio
+sidecar (``uvicorn local_server.app:create_app --factory``) concurrently, then
+prints the MCP and Studio URLs. Shutting down this script (Ctrl+C) terminates
+both processes.
+
+Usage:
+    python -m client.run
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import signal
+import socket
+import subprocess  # nosec B404 - launches only fixed child commands (see B603 notes)
+import sys
+import time
+
+MCP_PORT = 8000
+STUDIO_PORT = 8100
+
+REPO_ROOT = os.path.dirname(
+    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
+)
+SPA_DIST = os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "studio", "dist")
+SPA_BUILD_HINT = "Frontend not built — run `npm --prefix studio run build` to serve the Studio UI."
+
+
+def is_port_in_use(port: int) -> bool:
+    with socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as s:
+        return s.connect_ex(("localhost", port)) == 0
+
+
+def build_commands() -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
+    """Return the (mcp_server, sidecar) argv lists, both shell-free and fixed."""
+    mcp_command = [sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"]
+    sidecar_command = [
+        sys.executable,
+        "-m",
+        "uvicorn",
+        "local_server.app:create_app",
+        "--factory",
+        "--host",
+        "127.0.0.1",
+        "--port",
+        str(STUDIO_PORT),
+    ]
+    return mcp_command, sidecar_command
+
+
+def start_server() -> subprocess.Popen:
+    if is_port_in_use(MCP_PORT):
+        print(f"Error: Port {MCP_PORT} is already in use.")
+        print("Please stop any process running on this port and try again.")
+        sys.exit(1)
+
+    mcp_command, _ = build_commands()
+    print(f"Starting MCP server on http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp ...")
+    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
+    return subprocess.Popen(mcp_command)  # nosec B603
+
+
+def start_studio() -> subprocess.Popen:
+    if is_port_in_use(STUDIO_PORT):
+        print(f"Warning: Port {STUDIO_PORT} is already in use. The sidecar may fail to start.")
+
+    _, sidecar_command = build_commands()
+    print(f"Starting Living Studio sidecar on http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT} ...")
+    # Fixed command, no shell, no untrusted input.
+    return subprocess.Popen(sidecar_command)  # nosec B603
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    server = None
+    studio = None
+
+    def shutdown(signum=None, frame=None):
+        print("\nShutting down...")
+        if studio:
+            studio.terminate()
+        if server:
+            server.terminate()
+
+        try:
+            if studio:
+                studio.wait(timeout=5)
+            if server:
+                server.wait(timeout=5)
+        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+            if studio:
+                studio.kill()
+            if server:
+                server.kill()
+
+        print("✅ All processes stopped.")
+        sys.exit(0)
+
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, shutdown)
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown)
+
+    try:
+        server = start_server()
+        # Give the server a moment to bind its port before the sidecar connects
+        time.sleep(2)
+        studio = start_studio()
+
+        print("\nBoth processes are running.")
+        print(f"MCP Server   -> http://localhost:{MCP_PORT}/mcp")
+        print(f"Living Studio -> http://localhost:{STUDIO_PORT}")
+        if not os.path.isdir(SPA_DIST):
+            print(f"\n⚠️  {SPA_BUILD_HINT}")
+        print("\nPress Ctrl+C to stop both.\n")
+
+        # Wait for either process to exit unexpectedly
+        while True:
+            rc_server = server.poll()
+            rc_studio = studio.poll()
+
+            if rc_server is not None:
+                print(f"\nServer exited unexpectedly (code {rc_server}).")
+                break
+
+            if rc_studio is not None:
+                print(f"\nStudio sidecar exited unexpectedly (code {rc_studio}).")
+                break
+
+            time.sleep(1)
+
+    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
+        print(f"\nError: {e}")
+    finally:
+        shutdown()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""Tests for the launcher lifecycle: start, poll, and shut down both services."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import signal
+import subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pytest
+
+from client import run
+
+
+class _FakeProcess:
+    def __init__(self, poll_results: list[int | None] | None = None, wait_error=None) -> None:
+        self._poll_results = list(poll_results) if poll_results is not None else []
+        self._wait_error = wait_error
+        self.terminated = False
+        self.killed = False
+
+    def poll(self) -> int | None:
+        return self._poll_results.pop(0) if self._poll_results else None
+
+    def terminate(self) -> None:
+        self.terminated = True
+
+    def wait(self, timeout=None) -> int:
+        if self._wait_error is not None:
+            raise self._wait_error
+        return 0
+
+    def kill(self) -> None:
+        self.killed = True
+
+
+def _quiet_main(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.time, "sleep", lambda seconds: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.signal, "signal", lambda signum, handler: None)
+
+
+def test_start_server_exits_when_the_port_is_busy(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: True)
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
+        run.start_server()
+
+    assert exc_info.value.code == 1
+    assert f"Port {run.MCP_PORT} is already in use" in capsys.readouterr().out
+
+
+def test_start_server_launches_the_fixed_module(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
+    launched: list[list[str]] = []
+
+    def _popen(argv: list[str]) -> _FakeProcess:
+        launched.append(argv)
+        return _FakeProcess()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.subprocess, "Popen", _popen)
+
+    process = run.start_server()
+
+    assert isinstance(process, _FakeProcess)
+    assert launched == [[run.sys.executable, "-m", "mcp_server"]]
+    assert "Starting MCP server" in capsys.readouterr().out
+
+
+def test_start_studio_warns_but_still_launches(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
+    launched: list[list[str]] = []
+
+    def _popen(argv: list[str]) -> _FakeProcess:
+        launched.append(argv)
+        return _FakeProcess()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.subprocess, "Popen", _popen)
+
+    run.start_studio()
+
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert f"Port {run.STUDIO_PORT} is already in use" in output
+    assert launched == [run.build_commands()[1]]
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("exiting", ["server", "studio"])
+def test_main_reports_an_unexpected_exit_and_stops_both(monkeypatch, capsys, exiting) -> None:
+    _quiet_main(monkeypatch)
+    server = _FakeProcess([0] if exiting == "server" else [None])
+    studio = _FakeProcess([0] if exiting == "studio" else [None])
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_server", lambda: server)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_studio", lambda: studio)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "SPA_DIST", Path("/nonexistent/studio/dist"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
+        run.main()
+
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    expected = (
+        "Server exited unexpectedly"
+        if exiting == "server"
+        else "Studio sidecar exited unexpectedly"
+    )
+    assert exc_info.value.code == 0
+    assert expected in output
+    assert "All processes stopped." in output
+    assert "Frontend not built" in output
+    assert server.terminated is True
+    assert studio.terminated is True
+
+
+def test_main_waits_while_both_processes_are_running(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    sleeps: list[float] = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.time, "sleep", sleeps.append)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.signal, "signal", lambda signum, handler: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_server", lambda: _FakeProcess([None, 0]))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_studio", lambda: _FakeProcess([None, None]))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "SPA_DIST", Path("/nonexistent/studio/dist"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
+        run.main()
+
+    assert sleeps == [2, 1]
+
+
+def test_main_kills_processes_that_ignore_termination(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
+    _quiet_main(monkeypatch)
+    timeout = subprocess.TimeoutExpired(cmd="odi", timeout=5)
+    server = _FakeProcess([0], wait_error=timeout)
+    studio = _FakeProcess([None], wait_error=timeout)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_server", lambda: server)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_studio", lambda: studio)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "SPA_DIST", Path("/nonexistent/studio/dist"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
+        run.main()
+
+    assert server.killed is True
+    assert studio.killed is True
+
+
+def test_main_reports_startup_errors(monkeypatch, capsys) -> None:
+    _quiet_main(monkeypatch)
+
+    def _boom() -> None:
+        raise RuntimeError("boom")
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_server", _boom)
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
+        run.main()
+
+    output = capsys.readouterr().out
+    assert "Error: boom" in output
+    assert "All processes stopped." in output
+
+
+def test_main_installs_signal_handlers(monkeypatch) -> None:
+    seen: list[int] = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "is_port_in_use", lambda port: False)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.time, "sleep", lambda seconds: None)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run.signal, "signal", lambda signum, handler: seen.append(signum))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_server", lambda: _FakeProcess([0]))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "start_studio", lambda: _FakeProcess([None]))
+    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "SPA_DIST", Path("/nonexistent/studio/dist"))
+
+    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
+        run.main()
+
+    assert seen == [signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM]

+"""Ready-to-use MCP connector presets for common ODI workflows.
+
+Each preset captures everything needed to register a connector for a well-known
+MCP server: the endpoint, how it authenticates, and where its documentation
+lives. Presets are grouped by the five capability areas an outcome-driven
+innovation process needs, so a new workspace can be wired up with
+``agentic-odi connectors add mcp --preset <id>`` instead of hunting for URLs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import re
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+from connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+CapabilityArea = Literal[
+    "voice-of-customer",
+    "quantitative-data",
+    "market-intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment",
+    "knowledge-output",
+]
+
+AREA_LABELS: dict[CapabilityArea, str] = {
+    "voice-of-customer": "Voice of customer & qualitative research",
+    "quantitative-data": "Quantitative data & opportunity scoring",
+    "market-intelligence": "Market & competitive intelligence",
+    "strategy-alignment": "Product strategy & backlog alignment",
+    "knowledge-output": "Strategy & knowledge management output",
+}
+
+ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class UnknownPresetError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, preset_id: str) -> None:
+        self.preset_id = preset_id
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown preset: {preset_id} (try 'agentic-odi connectors catalog')")
+
+
+class UnknownAreaError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, area: str) -> None:
+        self.area = area
+        valid = ", ".join(AREA_LABELS)
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown capability area: {area} (expected one of: {valid})")
+
+
+class ConnectorPreset(BaseModel):
+    """A known MCP server plus the credentials it needs."""
+
+    id: str
+    label: str
+    area: CapabilityArea
+    summary: str
+    url: str
+    auth: Literal["none", "oauth"] = "none"
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    docs: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    def referenced_env_vars(self) -> set[str]:
+        """Environment variables the URL or headers interpolate with ``${VAR}``."""
+        found: set[str] = set()
+        for value in [self.url, *self.headers.values()]:
+            found.update(ENV_VAR_PATTERN.findall(value))
+        return found
+
+
+PRESETS: tuple[ConnectorPreset, ...] = (

+        url="https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://www.atlassian.com/platform/remote-mcp-server",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="miro",
+        label="Miro",
+        area="strategy-alignment",
+        summary="Outcome matrices and customer journey maps on a shared board.",
+        url="https://mcp.miro.com/",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.miro.com/docs/miro-mcp",
+    ),
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="figma",
+        label="Figma",
+        area="strategy-alignment",
+        summary="FigJam maps and design context for outcome workshops.",
+        url="https://mcp.figma.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://developers.figma.com/docs/figma-mcp-server/",
+    ),
+    # 5. Strategy & knowledge management output
+    ConnectorPreset(
+        id="slack",
+        label="Slack",
+        area="knowledge-output",
+        summary="Post opportunity-score digests and JTBD insights to channels.",
+        url="https://mcp.slack.com/mcp",
+        auth="oauth",
+        docs="https://docs.slack.dev/ai/",
+    ),
+)
+
+
+def list_presets(area: str | None = None) -> list[ConnectorPreset]:
+    """Return presets, optionally filtered by capability area."""
+    if area is None:
+        return list(PRESETS)
+    if area not in AREA_LABELS:
+        raise UnknownAreaError(area)
+    return [preset for preset in PRESETS if preset.area == area]
+
+
+def get_preset(preset_id: str) -> ConnectorPreset:
+    for preset in PRESETS:
+        if preset.id == preset_id:
+            return preset
+    raise UnknownPresetError(preset_id)
+
+
+def connector_config_from_preset(
+    preset: ConnectorPreset,
+    *,
+    name: str | None = None,
+    url: str | None = None,
+    tools: list[str] | None = None,
+    enabled: bool = True,
+) -> ConnectorConfig:
+    """Build a registry entry from a preset, allowing local overrides."""
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = {
+        "url": url or preset.url,
+        "auth": preset.auth,
+        "headers": dict(preset.headers),
+        "env_vars": list(preset.env_vars),
+        "tools": list(tools if tools is not None else preset.tools),
+    }
+    return ConnectorConfig(
+        name=name or preset.id,
+        kind="mcp",
+        enabled=enabled,
+        settings=settings,
+    )
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "AREA_LABELS",
+    "ENV_VAR_PATTERN",
+    "PRESETS",
+    "CapabilityArea",
+    "ConnectorPreset",
+    "UnknownAreaError",
+    "UnknownPresetError",
+    "connector_config_from_preset",
+    "get_preset",
+    "list_presets",
+]

+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+from connectors.mcp.connector import MCPClientConnector
+from connectors.models import ConnectorConfig, McpConnectorSettings
+from connectors.protocol import Connector
+from connectors.registry import UnknownConnectorKindError
+
+Builder = Callable[[ConnectorConfig], Connector]
+

+
+
+def register_kind(kind: str, builder: Builder) -> None:
+    """Register a builder for a connector kind (mcp today; others later)."""
+    _builders[kind] = builder
+
+
+def known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    return set(_builders)

+    try:

+"""MCP client connector that ingests tools and resources from an external server."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import os
+import re
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from fastmcp import Client, FastMCP
+from fastmcp.client.transports import StreamableHttpTransport
+
+from connectors.models import (
+    HealthStatus,
+    IngestBatch,
+    IngestRecord,
+    McpConnectorSettings,
+)
+from connectors.protocol import Connector
+
+_ENV_VAR_PATTERN = re.compile(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}")
+
+
+class MissingEnvironmentError(RuntimeError):
+    """Raised when a connector needs credentials that are not in the environment."""
+
+    def __init__(self, names: list[str]) -> None:
+        self.names = names
+        super().__init__("Missing environment variable(s): " + ", ".join(names))
+
+
+def _expand_env(value: str, environ: Mapping[str, str]) -> str:
+    return _ENV_VAR_PATTERN.sub(lambda match: environ.get(match.group(1), ""), value)
+
+
+def _to_dict(obj: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    if hasattr(obj, "model_dump"):
+        dumped = obj.model_dump(mode="json")
+        if isinstance(dumped, dict):
+            return dumped
+    return {"repr": repr(obj)}
+
+
+def _content_text(obj: Any) -> str:
+    parts: list[str] = []
+    content = getattr(obj, "content", None)
+    if content is None:
+        text = getattr(obj, "text", None)
+        return text if isinstance(text, str) else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+    for item in content:
+        text = getattr(item, "text", None)
+        if isinstance(text, str):
+            parts.append(text)
+    return "\n".join(parts) if parts else json.dumps(_to_dict(obj))
+
+
+class MCPClientConnector(Connector):
+    """Pulls catalog, resources, and optional tool results from an MCP server."""
+
+    kind = "mcp"
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        settings: McpConnectorSettings,
+        *,
+        server: FastMCP | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        self.settings = settings
+        self._server = server
+
+    def transport(self) -> StreamableHttpTransport | FastMCP:
+        """Build the MCP transport, resolving credentials from the environment."""
+        if self._server is not None:
+            return self._server
+        missing = sorted(name for name in self.settings.env_vars if not os.environ.get(name))
+        if missing:
+            raise MissingEnvironmentError(missing)
+        headers = {
+            key: _expand_env(value, os.environ) for key, value in self.settings.headers.items()
+        }
+        return StreamableHttpTransport(
+            url=_expand_env(self.settings.url, os.environ),
+            headers=headers or None,
+            auth="oauth" if self.settings.auth == "oauth" else None,
+        )
+
+    def _client(self) -> Client:
+        return Client(self.transport())
+
+    async def health(self) -> HealthStatus:
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=True,
+                message="reachable",
+                details={
+                    "tool_count": len(tools),
+                    "resource_count": len(resources),
+                },
+            )
+        except MissingEnvironmentError as exc:
+            return HealthStatus(
+                ok=False,
+                message=str(exc),
+                details={"missing_env": exc.names},
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            return HealthStatus(ok=False, message=str(exc))
+
+    async def ingest(self) -> IngestBatch:
+        batch = IngestBatch(connector_name=self.name)
+        try:
+            async with self._client() as client:
+                tools = await client.list_tools()
+                resources = await client.list_resources()
+                tool_dicts = [_to_dict(tool) for tool in tools]
+                resource_dicts = [_to_dict(resource) for resource in resources]
+                catalog_raw = {"tools": tool_dicts, "resources": resource_dicts}
+                batch.records.append(
+                    IngestRecord(
+                        source_name=self.name,
+                        source_kind=self.kind,
+                        item_type="catalog",
+                        name="mcp-catalog",
+                        content=json.dumps(catalog_raw, indent=2),
+                        raw=catalog_raw,
+                    )
+                )
+                for resource in resources:
+                    uri = str(getattr(resource, "uri", ""))
+                    name = str(getattr(resource, "name", None) or uri)
+                    try:
+                        contents = await client.read_resource(uri)
+                        content_text = "\n".join(
+                            getattr(item, "text", "") or "" for item in contents
+                        )
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="resource",
+                                name=name,
+                                content=content_text,
+                                raw={"uri": uri, "resource": _to_dict(resource)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to read resource {uri}: {exc}")
+                configured_tools = self.settings.tools
+                available = {str(getattr(tool, "name", "")) for tool in tools}
+                for tool_name in configured_tools:
+                    if tool_name not in available:
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Tool not found: {tool_name}")
+                        continue
+                    try:
+                        result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, {})
+                        batch.records.append(
+                            IngestRecord(
+                                source_name=self.name,
+                                source_kind=self.kind,
+                                item_type="tool_result",
+                                name=tool_name,
+                                content=_content_text(result),
+                                raw={"tool": tool_name, "result": _to_dict(result)},
+                            )
+                        )
+                    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+                        batch.errors.append(f"Failed to call tool {tool_name}: {exc}")
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            batch.errors.append(str(exc))
+        return batch

+"""Shared Pydantic models for external connectors and ingest records."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from typing import Any, Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
+
+ItemType = Literal["resource", "tool_result", "catalog"]
+McpAuthMode = Literal["none", "oauth"]
+
+
+class HealthStatus(BaseModel):
+    ok: bool
+    message: str
+    details: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestRecord(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    source_name: str
+    source_kind: str
+    item_type: ItemType
+    name: str
+    content: str
+    raw: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+
+
+class IngestBatch(BaseModel):
+    connector_name: str
+    records: list[IngestRecord] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class McpConnectorSettings(BaseModel):
+    """Connection details for an MCP server.
+
+    ``url`` and ``headers`` may interpolate environment variables with
+    ``${VAR}`` so registry files never hold tokens. ``env_vars`` names the
+    variables that must be present before connecting.
+    """
+
+    url: str
+    tools: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    auth: McpAuthMode = "none"
+    headers: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    env_vars: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class ConnectorConfig(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    kind: str
+    enabled: bool = True
+    settings: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

+"""JSON-backed registry of named connector configurations."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from connectors.models import ConnectorConfig
+
+
+class UnknownConnectorKindError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, kind: str) -> None:
+        self.kind = kind
+        super().__init__(f"Unknown connector kind: {kind}")
+
+
+class DuplicateConnectorError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector already exists: {name}")
+
+
+class ConnectorNotFoundError(ValueError):
+    def __init__(self, name: str) -> None:
+        self.name = name
+        super().__init__(f"Connector not found: {name}")
+
+
+def _known_kinds() -> set[str]:
+    from connectors.factory import known_kinds
+
+    return known_kinds()
+
+
+class ConnectorRegistry:
+    """Persists connector configs to a JSON file."""
+
+    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        self.path = path
+
+    def add(self, config: ConnectorConfig) -> None:
+        if config.kind not in _known_kinds():
+            raise UnknownConnectorKindError(config.kind)
+        connectors = self._load()
+        if any(existing.name == config.name for existing in connectors):
+            raise DuplicateConnectorError(config.name)
+        connectors.append(config)
+        self._save(connectors)
+
+    def list_all(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        return self._load()
+
+    def get(self, name: str) -> ConnectorConfig:
+        for config in self._load():
+            if config.name == name:
+                return config
+        raise ConnectorNotFoundError(name)
+
+    def _load(self) -> list[ConnectorConfig]:
+        if not self.path.exists():
+            return []
+        with self.path.open(encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            payload: dict[str, Any] = json.load(handle)
+        raw_connectors = payload.get("connectors", [])
+        return [ConnectorConfig.model_validate(item) for item in raw_connectors]
+
+    def _save(self, connectors: list[ConnectorConfig]) -> None:
+        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        payload = {"connectors": [item.model_dump(mode="json") for item in connectors]}
+        with self.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(payload, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")

+"""In-memory ingest sink owned by the connectors package."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from connectors.models import IngestBatch, IngestRecord
+
+
+class IngestSink:
+    """Stores ingested batches for the current process."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._batches: list[IngestBatch] = []
+
+    def append(self, batch: IngestBatch) -> None:
+        self._batches.append(batch)
+
+    def batches(self) -> list[IngestBatch]:
+        return list(self._batches)
+
+    def records(self) -> list[IngestRecord]:
+        return [record for batch in self._batches for record in batch.records]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self._batches.clear()
+
+
+_default_sink = IngestSink()
+
+
+def get_default_sink() -> IngestSink:
+    return _default_sink

+"""Append-only Intent Store (CTO specification)."""
+
+import json
+import sqlite3
+from datetime import datetime
+
+
+class IntentStore:
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str = "intent_store.db") -> None:
+        # Connect to SQLite in WAL mode for high-performance concurrency
+        self.conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
+        self.conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;")
+        self._init_db()
+
+    def _init_db(self) -> None:
+        """Creates an immutable, append-only event table."""
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                """
+                CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
+                    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+                    timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
+                    payload TEXT NOT NULL
+                )
+            """
+            )
+
+    def append(self, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
+        """Appends a new event to the stream (Immutable write)."""
+        timestamp = datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
+        payload_json = json.dumps(payload)
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute(
+                "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
+                (timestamp, event_type, payload_json),
+            )
+
+    def get_stream(self) -> list[dict]:
+        """Retrieves the full chronological event stream for AI reasoning."""
+        cursor = self.conn.cursor()
+        cursor.execute("SELECT id, timestamp, event_type, payload FROM events ORDER BY id ASC")
+        return [
+            {
+                "id": row[0],
+                "timestamp": row[1],
+                "type": row[2],
+                "payload": json.loads(row[3]) if row[3] else {},
+            }
+            for row in cursor.fetchall()
+        ]
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        """Clear all events (for testing)."""
+        with self.conn:
+            self.conn.execute("DELETE FROM events")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self.conn.close()

+ODI_ASSISTANT_PROMPT = """You are an expert in Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI). Your purpose is to help users discover, define, and prioritize high-value jobs, desired outcomes, and opportunities."""
+
+ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES = """## Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) — Stage-by-Stage Tool Guide
+
+Follow this sequence when guiding a user through the ODI process:
+
+### Stage 1: Define Intent (Job-to-be-Done)
+- **When**: Always start here if no Job exists.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What is the main task or goal your customer is trying to accomplish?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_job(name, description)` — Create the Job once identified.
+  - `get_jobs()` — Check if a relevant Job already exists before creating a new one.
+  - `get_job(job_id)` — Retrieve details of a specific existing Job.
+
+### Stage 2: Capture Desired Outcomes
+- **When**: After a Job is defined. Outcomes come BEFORE steps or solutions.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What does success look like? What should happen faster, more reliably, or more consistently?'
+- **Outcome statement format**: 'Minimize/Maximize the [metric] when [context].'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_outcome(job_id, statement, importance, satisfaction)` — Capture each desired outcome with scores.
+  - `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review all outcomes captured for a Job.
+
+### Stage 3: Calculate Opportunity Scores
+- **When**: After outcomes have importance and satisfaction scores.
+- **Formula**: Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)
+- **Scores > 10** indicate high innovation opportunity. Guide the user to focus efforts there.
+- **Tools to use**: `get_outcomes(job_id)` — Review opportunity_score field on each outcome.
+
+### Stage 4: Build the Job Map
+- **When**: After key outcomes are captured. Use to organize the job execution context.
+- **Ask the user**: 'What are the key phases or steps the customer takes when doing this job?'
+- **Tools to use**:
+  - `add_step(job_id, name, order)` — Add each chronological step.
+  - `get_job_map(job_id)` — View the complete ordered job map.
+
+### General Rule
+Never skip stages. Always confirm the user has a Job defined (Stage 1) before capturing Outcomes (Stage 2), and always capture Outcomes (Stage 2) before building the Job Map (Stage 4)."""
+
+
+def get_odi_framework_guidelines() -> str:
+    return ODI_FRAMEWORK_GUIDELINES
+
+
+CAPABILITIES = """Here is what I can help you with as your Agentic ODI assistant:
+

+"""Core domain models for Agentic ODI."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from enum import Enum
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, computed_field
+
+
+class Direction(str, Enum):
+    MINIMIZE = "minimize"
+    MAXIMIZE = "maximize"
+
+
+class BusinessImpactCategory(str, Enum):
+    REVENUE_GROWTH = "revenue_growth"
+    COST_REDUCTION = "cost_reduction"
+    RETENTION = "retention"
+    RISK_MITIGATION = "risk_mitigation"
+    OPERATIONAL_EFFICIENCY = "operational_efficiency"
+    COMPLIANCE = "compliance"
+    BRAND_REPUTATION = "brand_reputation"
+    OTHER = "other"
+
+
+def compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
+    """ODI Opportunity Score = importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)."""
+    return float(importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0.0))
+
+
+class Job(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the Job-to-be-Done")
+    description: str | None = Field(None, description="Detailed description of the Job")
+
+
+class Step(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this step belongs to")
+    name: str = Field(..., description="The name of the job step")
+    order: int = Field(..., description="The chronological order of this step in the job map")
+
+
+class Outcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable")
+    statement: str = Field(
+        ..., description="The desired outcome statement (e.g., 'Minimize the time it takes to...')"
+    )
+    importance: float | None = Field(None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Importance score (1-10)")
+    satisfaction: float | None = Field(
+        None, ge=1.0, le=10.0, description="Current satisfaction score (1-10)"
+    )
+    opportunity_score: float | None = Field(
+        None, description="Opportunity score (Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0))"
+    )
+
+
+class ValueMetric(BaseModel):
+    name: str
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class CustomerValue(BaseModel):
+    direction: Direction
+    unit_of_measure: str
+    object_of_control: str
+    contextual_clarifier: str | None = None
+    statement: str
+    importance: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    satisfaction: float = Field(ge=1.0, le=10.0)
+    value_metrics: list[ValueMetric] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(self.importance, self.satisfaction)
+
+
+class BusinessValue(BaseModel):
+    category: BusinessImpactCategory
+    statement: str
+    detail: str | None = None
+    estimated_annual_value: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0)
+    confidence: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
+
+
+class CustomerOutcome(BaseModel):
+    id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
+    job_id: str = Field(..., description="The ID of the Job this outcome relates to")
+    step_id: str | None = Field(
+        default=None, description="The ID of the specific Step, if applicable"
+    )
+    customer_value: CustomerValue
+    business_value: BusinessValue
+
+    @computed_field
+    @property
+    def opportunity_score(self) -> float:
+        return self.customer_value.opportunity_score

+"""Repository interfaces and in-memory implementation."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Protocol
+
+from core.models import CustomerOutcome, Job, Outcome, Step
+
+
+class Repository(Protocol):
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job: ...
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]: ...
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None: ...
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step: ...
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]: ...
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome: ...
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]: ...
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome: ...
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]: ...
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None: ...
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool: ...
+    def clear(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+class InMemoryRepository:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs: dict[str, Job] = {}
+        self.steps: dict[str, Step] = {}
+        self.outcomes: dict[str, Outcome] = {}
+        self.customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome] = {}
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job:
+        self.jobs[job.id] = job
+        return job
+
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return list(self.jobs.values())
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.jobs.get(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step:
+        self.steps[step.id] = step
+        return step
+
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        return [s for s in self.steps.values() if s.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome:
+        self.outcomes[outcome.id] = outcome
+        return outcome
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        outs = [o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            outs = [o for o in outs if o.step_id == step_id]
+        return outs
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        self.customer_outcomes[co.id] = co
+        return co
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        return self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        if job_id is None:
+            return list(self.customer_outcomes.values())
+        return [co for co in self.customer_outcomes.values() if co.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        co = self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            return None
+        current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        new_co = co.model_validate(current)
+        self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id] = new_co
+        return new_co
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.customer_outcomes:
+            del self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs.clear()
+        self.steps.clear()
+        self.outcomes.clear()
+        self.customer_outcomes.clear()

+"""Service layer implementing business logic."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import uuid
+from typing import Any
+
+from core.models import (
+    BusinessValue,
+    CustomerOutcome,
+    CustomerValue,
+    Job,
+    Outcome,
+    Step,
+    compute_opportunity_score,
+)
+from core.repository import Repository
+
+
+class JobNotFoundError(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, job_id: str) -> None:
+        self.job_id = job_id
+        super().__init__(job_id)
+
+
+class CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(Exception):
+    def __init__(self, outcome_id: str) -> None:
+        self.outcome_id = outcome_id
+        super().__init__(outcome_id)
+
+
+class ValueOutOfRangeError(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class ODIService:
+    def __init__(self, repo: Repository) -> None:
+        self.repo = repo
+
+    def add_job(self, name: str, description: str | None = None) -> Job:
+        job = Job(name=name, description=description)
+        return self.repo.add_job(job)
+
+    def get_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return self.repo.list_jobs()
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.repo.get_job(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, job_id: str, name: str, order: int) -> Step:
+        step = Step(id=str(uuid.uuid4()), job_id=job_id, name=name, order=order)
+        return self.repo.add_step(step)
+
+    def get_job_map(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        steps = self.repo.get_steps_for_job(job_id)
+        return sorted(steps, key=lambda s: s.order)
+
+    def add_outcome(
+        self,
+        job_id: str,
+        statement: str,
+        importance: float | None = None,
+        satisfaction: float | None = None,
+        step_id: str | None = None,
+    ) -> Outcome:
+        if importance is not None and not (1.0 <= importance <= 10.0):
+            raise ValueOutOfRangeError()
+        if satisfaction is not None and not (1.0 <= satisfaction <= 10.0):
+            raise ValueOutOfRangeError()
+        opportunity_score = None
+        if importance is not None and satisfaction is not None:
+            opportunity_score = compute_opportunity_score(importance, satisfaction)
+        outcome = Outcome(
+            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
+            job_id=job_id,
+            step_id=step_id,
+            statement=statement,
+            importance=importance,
+            satisfaction=satisfaction,
+            opportunity_score=opportunity_score,
+        )
+        return self.repo.add_outcome(outcome)
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        return self.repo.get_outcomes(job_id, step_id)
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(
+        self,
+        job_id: str,
+        customer_value: CustomerValue | dict[str, Any],
+        business_value: BusinessValue | dict[str, Any],
+        step_id: str | None = None,
+    ) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        if isinstance(customer_value, dict):
+            cv = CustomerValue.model_validate(customer_value)
+        else:
+            cv = customer_value
+        if isinstance(business_value, dict):
+            bv = BusinessValue.model_validate(business_value)
+        else:
+            bv = business_value
+        co = CustomerOutcome(
+            id=str(uuid.uuid4()),
+            job_id=job_id,
+            step_id=step_id,
+            customer_value=cv,
+            business_value=bv,
+        )
+        return self.repo.add_customer_outcome(co)
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        co = self.repo.get_customer_outcome(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+        return co
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        return self.repo.list_customer_outcomes(job_id)
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict[str, Any]) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        res = self.repo.update_customer_outcome(outcome_id, updates)
+        if not res:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+        return res
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> None:
+        ok = self.repo.delete_customer_outcome(outcome_id)
+        if not ok:
+            raise CustomerOutcomeNotFoundError(outcome_id)
+
+    def compute_opportunity(self, importance: float, satisfaction: float) -> float:
+        return compute_opportunity_score(importance, satisfaction)

+"""SQLite-backed repository using append-only IntentStore for events/audit."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from typing import Any
+
+from pydantic import ValidationError
+
+from core.intent_store import IntentStore
+from core.models import CustomerOutcome, Job, Outcome, Step
+from core.repository import Repository
+
+
+class SQLiteRepository(Repository):
+    def __init__(self, db_path: str | None = None) -> None:
+        if db_path is None:
+            db_path = os.environ.get("AGENTIC_ODI_DB", os.path.expanduser("~/.agentic-odi/odi.db"))
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(db_path) or ".", exist_ok=True)
+        self.store = IntentStore(db_path)
+        # For compatibility with existing semantics, we also maintain a materialized
+        # view in memory for fast reads (in-memory snapshot) - simple approach for now.
+        self._load_snapshot()
+
+    def _load_snapshot(self) -> None:
+        self.jobs: dict[str, Job] = {}
+        self.steps: dict[str, Step] = {}
+        self.outcomes: dict[str, Outcome] = {}
+        self.customer_outcomes: dict[str, CustomerOutcome] = {}
+        for ev in self.store.get_stream():
+            et = ev["type"]
+            p = ev["payload"]
+            if et == "JOB_CREATED":
+                self.jobs[p["id"]] = Job.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "STEP_CREATED":
+                self.steps[p["id"]] = Step.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "OUTCOME_CREATED":
+                self.outcomes[p["id"]] = Outcome.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_CREATED":
+                self.customer_outcomes[p["id"]] = CustomerOutcome.model_validate(p)
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED":
+                cid = p["id"]
+                co = self.customer_outcomes.get(cid)
+                if co is not None:
+                    current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+                    current.update(p.get("updates", {}))
+                    try:
+                        self.customer_outcomes[cid] = co.model_validate(current)
+                    except ValidationError:
+                        pass
+            elif et == "CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_DELETED":
+                cid = p["id"]
+                self.customer_outcomes.pop(cid, None)
+        # also snapshot jobs/steps/outcomes? we emitted above
+
+    def add_job(self, job: Job) -> Job:
+        self.store.append("JOB_CREATED", job.model_dump())
+        self.jobs[job.id] = job
+        return job
+
+    def list_jobs(self) -> list[Job]:
+        return list(self.jobs.values())
+
+    def get_job(self, job_id: str) -> Job | None:
+        return self.jobs.get(job_id)
+
+    def add_step(self, step: Step) -> Step:
+        self.store.append("STEP_CREATED", step.model_dump())
+        self.steps[step.id] = step
+        return step
+
+    def get_steps_for_job(self, job_id: str) -> list[Step]:
+        return [s for s in self.steps.values() if s.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def add_outcome(self, outcome: Outcome) -> Outcome:
+        self.store.append("OUTCOME_CREATED", outcome.model_dump())
+        self.outcomes[outcome.id] = outcome
+        return outcome
+
+    def get_outcomes(self, job_id: str, step_id: str | None = None) -> list[Outcome]:
+        outs = [o for o in self.outcomes.values() if o.job_id == job_id]
+        if step_id is not None:
+            outs = [o for o in outs if o.step_id == step_id]
+        return outs
+
+    def add_customer_outcome(self, co: CustomerOutcome) -> CustomerOutcome:
+        self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_CREATED", co.model_dump())
+        self.customer_outcomes[co.id] = co
+        return co
+
+    def get_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        return self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+
+    def list_customer_outcomes(self, job_id: str | None = None) -> list[CustomerOutcome]:
+        if job_id is None:
+            return list(self.customer_outcomes.values())
+        return [co for co in self.customer_outcomes.values() if co.job_id == job_id]
+
+    def update_customer_outcome(
+        self, outcome_id: str, updates: dict[str, Any]
+    ) -> CustomerOutcome | None:
+        co = self.customer_outcomes.get(outcome_id)
+        if not co:
+            return None
+        current = co.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
+        current.update(updates)
+        try:
+            new_co = co.model_validate(current)
+        except ValidationError:
+            return None
+        self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_UPDATED", {"id": outcome_id, "updates": updates})
+        self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id] = new_co
+        return new_co
+
+    def delete_customer_outcome(self, outcome_id: str) -> bool:
+        if outcome_id in self.customer_outcomes:
+            self.store.append("CUSTOMER_OUTCOME_DELETED", {"id": outcome_id})
+            del self.customer_outcomes[outcome_id]
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def clear(self) -> None:
+        self.store.clear()
+        self._load_snapshot()

+"""Tests for the append-only Intent Store."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from core.intent_store import IntentStore
+
+
+def test_append_and_get_stream_return_events_in_order(tmp_path) -> None:
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "events.db"))
+    try:
+        store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "job-1"})
+        store.append("STEP_CREATED", {"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"})
+
+        stream = store.get_stream()
+    finally:
+        store.close()
+
+    assert [event["type"] for event in stream] == ["JOB_CREATED", "STEP_CREATED"]
+    assert [event["payload"] for event in stream] == [
+        {"id": "job-1"},
+        {"id": "step-1", "job_id": "job-1"},
+    ]
+    assert [event["id"] for event in stream] == [1, 2]
+    assert all(event["timestamp"] for event in stream)
+
+
+def test_clear_removes_every_event(tmp_path) -> None:
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "events.db"))
+    try:
+        store.append("JOB_CREATED", {"id": "job-1"})
+        store.clear()
+        assert store.get_stream() == []
+    finally:
+        store.close()
+
+
+def test_get_stream_treats_blank_payload_as_empty_dict(tmp_path) -> None:
+    store = IntentStore(str(tmp_path / "events.db"))
+    try:
+        store.conn.execute(
+            "INSERT INTO events (timestamp, event_type, payload) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
+            ("2026-01-01T00:00:00", "LEGACY", ""),
+        )
+        store.conn.commit()
+
+        assert store.get_stream()[0]["payload"] == {}
+    finally:
+        store.close()

+"""Tests for core domain models and ODI opportunity scoring."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import pytest
+
+from core.models import (
+    BusinessImpactCategory,
+    BusinessValue,
+    CustomerOutcome,
+    CustomerValue,
+    Direction,
+    ValueMetric,
+    compute_opportunity_score,
+)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("importance", "satisfaction", "expected"),
+    [
+        (8.0, 4.0, 12.0),
+        (5.0, 5.0, 5.0),
+        (3.0, 9.0, 3.0),
+        (10.0, 1.0, 19.0),
+    ],
+)
+def test_compute_opportunity_score(importance: float, satisfaction: float, expected: float) -> None:
+    assert compute_opportunity_score(importance, satisfaction) == expected
+
+
+def _customer_value(**overrides: object) -> CustomerValue:
+    data: dict[str, object] = {
+        "direction": Direction.MINIMIZE,
+        "unit_of_measure": "minutes",
+        "object_of_control": "time to resolve a support ticket",
+        "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to resolve a support ticket",
+        "importance": 8.0,
+        "satisfaction": 4.0,
+    }
+    data.update(overrides)
+    return CustomerValue(**data)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
+
+
+def test_customer_value_opportunity_score_is_computed() -> None:
+    assert _customer_value().opportunity_score == 12.0
+
+
+def test_value_metric_opportunity_score_is_computed() -> None:
+    metric = ValueMetric(
+        name="resolution time",
+        direction=Direction.MINIMIZE,
+        unit_of_measure="minutes",
+        importance=9.0,
+        satisfaction=2.0,
+    )
+    assert metric.opportunity_score == 16.0
+
+
+def test_customer_outcome_delegates_opportunity_score() -> None:
+    outcome = CustomerOutcome(
+        job_id="job-1",
+        customer_value=_customer_value(importance=6.0, satisfaction=1.0),
+        business_value=BusinessValue(
+            category=BusinessImpactCategory.COST_REDUCTION,
+            statement="Reduce support cost",
+        ),
+    )
+    assert outcome.opportunity_score == 11.0

+            statement="Reduce support cost",
+        ),

+

+    repo = InMemoryRepository()
+    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o-1", job_id="job-1", step_id="step-1", statement="one"))
+    repo.add_outcome(Outcome(id="o-2", job_id="job-1", step_id="step-2", statement="two"))

+    assert [o.id for o in repo.get_outcomes("job-1", step_id="step-1")] == ["o-1"]

+    assert [co.id for co in repo.list_customer_outcomes()] == ["co-1", "co-2"]

+

+

+    assert repo.get_steps_for_job(job.id) == []
+    assert repo.get_outcomes(job.id) == []

+)

+@pytest.fixture

+def _customer_value() -> CustomerValue:

 # CLI Reference
 
 The `agentic-odi` CLI is a [`Typer`](https://github.com/fastapi/typer)-based
 command-line interface for working with Agentic ODI without a chat UI. It
 provides an interactive chat mode plus version, update, and data commands. Data
 commands are **local-first**: they read and write a SQLite store with no server
 required, and switch to a remote MCP server with `--backend mcp`.
 
 Install the workspace first if you have not already:
 
 ```bash
 uv sync --all-packages
 ```
 
 ## Launching
 
 ```bash
-python -m agentic_odi_cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
-python -m agentic_odi_cli --help      # show available options and commands
-python -m agentic_odi_cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
+python -m cli --version   # print the Agentic ODI version
+python -m cli --help      # show available options and commands
+python -m cli             # start interactive chat in a terminal (help when piped)
 ```
 
 A console script is also installed, so `agentic-odi --version` works the same way.
 
 ## Global options
 
 | Option | Environment variable | Default | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | `--backend local\|mcp` | `AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND` | `local` | Run in-process against SQLite, or call a remote MCP server. |
 | `--db PATH` | `AGENTIC_ODI_DB` | `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db` | Store path for the `local` backend. |
 | `--mcp-url URL` | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | Server URL for the `mcp` backend. |
 
 Data commands print readable tables and blocks by default; add `--json` for
 machine-readable output. Diagnostics go to stderr and failures exit non-zero
 (`0` success, `1` error, `2` usage error).
 
 ## Interactive chat
 
-`agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts an
-offline-first interactive REPL. The session always boots, even when no model or
-MCP server is reachable — a yellow warning is shown for any unavailable service,
-and free-text messages return a friendly nudge until you connect.
+`agentic-odi chat` (or simply `agentic-odi` in a terminal) starts a
+conversational session against the MCP server and an OpenAI-compatible LLM.
+Responses stream to the terminal, and the assistant can call the ODI MCP tools
+as it talks.
 
 ```bash
 agentic-odi chat
 agentic-odi chat --model local-tools-model --mcp-url http://localhost:8000/mcp
 ```
 
-### Connection settings
+Before starting, run the MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`) and point the chat
+at an OpenAI-compatible model endpoint. The chat reads the same environment
+variables as the Living Studio:
 
-The chat resolves settings in priority order:
-**CLI flag → environment variable → persisted profile → built-in default.**
-
 | Variable | Default | CLI flag |
 |---|---|---|
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8001/v1` | `--base-url` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MODEL` | `local-tools-model` | `--model` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_API_KEY` | `local` | `--api-key` |
 | `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | `--mcp-url` |
 
-The **persisted profile** is stored at
-`~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json`. You can create or update it from
-within the session using `/connect`.
+Inside the session, `/help` lists the commands, `/tools` lists the MCP tools the
+assistant can call, `/clear` resets the conversation, and `/exit` (or `/quit`)
+ends the session.
 
-### Slash commands
-
-| Command | Description |
-|---|---|
-| `/help` | Show all available commands |
-| `/status` | Show current model, base URL, and MCP server with connection status |
-| `/connect` | Launch the wizard: provider → URL → API key → model → MCP URL → save |
-| `/model <name>` | Hot-swap to a different model mid-session |
-| `/mcp <url>` | Reconnect to a different MCP server mid-session |
-| `/tools` | List the MCP tools the assistant can call |
-| `/clear` | Reset conversation history (keeps connection) |
-| `/exit` | Quit the session (also `/quit`) |
-
-### /connect wizard
-
-`/connect` walks you through configuring your LLM provider interactively:
-
-1. **Provider** — choose `openai`, `anthropic`, `local`, or `other`
-2. **Base URL** — preset filled for known providers; override freely
-3. **API key** — input is hidden via `getpass`
-4. **Model** — sensible default per provider
-5. **MCP URL** — defaults to the current value
-6. **Save to profile?** — writes `~/.config/agentic-odi/llm_profile.json` so settings persist across sessions
-
-The wizard can be cancelled at any step with Ctrl-C.
-
 > [!NOTE]
 > Chat is the only CLI mode that needs an LLM endpoint. The `customer-outcomes`
 > and `connectors` commands keep working without one.
 
-## Manage Jobs, Steps, and desired Outcomes
-
-Every ODI entity has the same create/read/update/delete surface in the CLI and
-the MCP server. Jobs hold Steps (the Job Map) and desired Outcomes; deleting a
-Job cascades to both.
-
-```bash
-# Jobs
-agentic-odi jobs add --name "Onboard a customer" --description "First 30 days"
-agentic-odi jobs list
-agentic-odi jobs get <job-id>
-agentic-odi jobs update <job-id> --name "Onboard a new customer"
-agentic-odi jobs delete <job-id> --yes
-
-# Steps (Job Map)
-agentic-odi steps add --job-id <job-id> --name "Prepare environment" --order 1
-agentic-odi steps list --job-id <job-id>
-agentic-odi steps get <step-id>
-agentic-odi steps update <step-id> --order 2
-agentic-odi steps delete <step-id> --yes
-
-# Desired Outcomes
-agentic-odi desired-outcomes add --job-id <job-id>   --statement "Minimize the time it takes to get a working environment"   --importance 8 --satisfaction 4
-agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
-agentic-odi desired-outcomes get <outcome-id>
-agentic-odi desired-outcomes update <outcome-id> --satisfaction 6
-agentic-odi desired-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
-```
-
-Add `--json` to any command for machine-readable output.
-
-## Evidence
-
-Evidence is research captured from connectors (or entered by hand) and linked to
-a Job, Step, or desired Outcome. Records can later be promoted into ODI
-artifacts — the bridge from research to the model, without hand-copying.
-
-```bash
-# Capture a record by hand
-agentic-odi evidence add \
-  --source-name "interview" --source-kind manual \
-  --name "Support lead" \
-  --content "Setup takes two days for every new engineer" \
-  --job-id <job-id>
-
-# Read and delete
-agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id>
-agentic-odi evidence list --job-id <job-id> --json
-agentic-odi evidence get <evidence-id>
-agentic-odi evidence delete <evidence-id> --yes
-
-# Promote into the ODI model
-agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to job
-agentic-odi evidence promote <evidence-id> --to outcome --job-id <job-id>
-```
-
-`connectors ingest --job-id <job-id>` maps every evidence-bearing record in the
-ingested batch into evidence in one step.
-
-## Schema and scoring
-
-```bash
-agentic-odi schema            # canonical JSON schema for every ODI entity
-agentic-odi score 8 2         # ODI opportunity score → 14.00
-```
-
 ## Manage Customer Outcomes
 
 Customer Outcomes link customer value to business value. The `local` backend
 writes to the shared SQLite store with no server required; add `--backend mcp`
-to route through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). The group is also
+to route through a running MCP server (`python -m mcp_server`). The group is also
 available under its historical name `outcomes`.
 
 ```bash
 # Add a Customer Outcome
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
   --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
   --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
   --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 \
   --category cost_reduction \
   --business-statement "Saves engineering hours and reduces early churn"
 
-# Attach value metrics: repeatable JSON objects
-agentic-odi customer-outcomes add --job-id <job-id> \
-  --direction minimize --unit "time" --object "to resolve setup errors" \
-  --statement "Minimize the time to resolve environment setup errors when onboarding" \
-  --importance 8.8 --satisfaction 3.2 --category cost_reduction \
-  --business-statement "Saves engineering hours" \
-  --value-metric '{"name":"first response","direction":"minimize","unit_of_measure":"minutes","importance":7,"satisfaction":3}'
-
 # List outcomes (optionally filtered, or as JSON)
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --job-id <job-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes list --json
 
 # Get, update, delete
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes get <outcome-id>
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes update <outcome-id> --importance 9.0
 agentic-odi customer-outcomes delete <outcome-id> --yes
 
 # Compute an ODI Opportunity Score (top-level, also under the group)
 agentic-odi score 8 2
 agentic-odi outcomes score 8 2
 ```
 
 `score` applies the ODI opportunity formula,
 `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.
 
 Set `AGENTIC_ODI_MCP_URL` (or `--mcp-url`) to point to a non-default server when
 using `--backend mcp` (default: `http://localhost:8000/mcp`).
 
 ## Connectors
 
 The `connectors` group manages external MCP integrations. See
 [External Connectors](connectors.md) for presets, the connector registry, and
 ingest behavior.
 
 ```bash
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+python -m cli connectors catalog
+python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m cli connectors list
+python -m cli connectors health --name github
+python -m cli connectors ingest --name github
 ```
 
 ## Updates
 
 `odi update` checks for and installs a new binary release. Auto-update is on by
 default; disable it with `--no-update` for one run or
 `AGENTIC_ODI_NO_UPDATE=1` globally. See [Installation](installation.md).

 # External Connectors (MCP Ingest)
 
 Connectors are named integrations stored in `.agentic-odi/connectors.json` (or a
 path you pass with `--config` / `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_FILE`). The first kind is
 `mcp`: Agentic ODI acts as an MCP **client** and pulls catalog, resources, and
 optional tool results from an external MCP **server**.
 
 ## Presets
 
 The fastest way to connect is a preset. `connectors catalog` lists every
 built-in preset, grouped by the capability area it serves:
 
 ```bash
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors catalog --json
+python -m cli connectors catalog                          # all presets
+python -m cli connectors catalog --area strategy-alignment
+python -m cli connectors catalog --json
 ```
 
 | Capability area (`--area`) | Presets |
 |---|---|
 | Voice of customer & qualitative research (`voice-of-customer`) | `notion`, `gong`, `fireflies`, `intercom`, `confluence` |
 | Quantitative data & opportunity scoring (`quantitative-data`) | `posthog`, `amplitude`, `mixpanel` |
 | Market & competitive intelligence (`market-intelligence`) | `exa`, `tavily` |
 | Product strategy & backlog alignment (`strategy-alignment`) | `linear`, `github`, `jira`, `miro`, `figma` |
 | Strategy & knowledge management output (`knowledge-output`) | `slack` |
 
 Register one with `--preset`; `--name` defaults to the preset id:
 
 ```bash
 # Token-based preset: export the variable it needs first
 export GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_...
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset github
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors health --name github
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors ingest --name github
+python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset github
+python -m cli connectors health --name github
+python -m cli connectors ingest --name github
 
 # OAuth-based preset: the browser consent flow starts on first use
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
+python -m cli connectors add mcp --preset notion
 ```
 
 Credentials never enter the registry. Presets that use API keys store `${VAR}`
 placeholders that are resolved from the environment when a connection is
 opened, and `connectors health` names any variable that is missing. `--url`
 overrides the endpoint (self-hosted or proxied deployments) and `--tool` still
 selects which tools to call during ingest.
 
 Custom servers keep working the same way:
 
 ```bash
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
-python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors list
+python -m cli connectors add mcp --name internal --url https://mcp.internal.example/mcp --tool latest_quote
+python -m cli connectors list
 ```
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > Presets cover MCP servers with a hosted endpoint. Servers you run yourself
 > (Snowflake, BigQuery, Google Drive, Brave Search, and similar) are added with
 > an explicit `--url`. The catalog lives in
-> `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py`.
+> `connectors/src/connectors/catalog.py`.
 
 > [!NOTE]
 > OAuth tokens are cached in memory for the life of one CLI process, so an OAuth
 > preset may ask for consent again on the next `connectors health` or
 > `connectors ingest`. Prefer a token-based preset where the server offers one.
 
 ## Ingest behavior
 
 Ingested records are normalized (`catalog`, `resource`, `tool_result`) and
 appended to the in-process ingest sink. They are **not** written into the ODI
 jobs/outcomes store — mapping ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts is still on
 the [roadmap](roadmap.md).
 
 Additional kinds (REST, webhooks, and so on) can register against the same
 `Connector` protocol later.

-## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker
-
-Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
-Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
-the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
-through a free, account-less
-[Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).
-
-`wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
-first for `/api/*`; `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
-`SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
-sidecar's CORS list is not involved.
-
-```bash
-# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
-npm --prefix apps/studio ci
-npm --prefix apps/studio run build
-
-# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
-python scripts/dev.py
-
-# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
-cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
-# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints
-
-# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
-npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
-npx wrangler deploy
-```
-
-Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):
-
-| Setting | Value |
-|---|---|
-| Root directory | `/` |
-| Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
-| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |
-
-A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
-`wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.
-
-> [!NOTE]
-> The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
-> `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
-> change on every restart — update the secret with
-> `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
-> OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
-> and impact simulation work without one.
